question: What does the term 'medicalisation of FGM' mean in clinical practice?

options.A: Administering antibiotics to heal infected genital wounds
options.B: Providing surgical reconstruction for women living with FGM
options.C: Performing FGM using trained health personnel and sterile tools
options.D: Treating FGM complications in a modern hospital ward

explanation: Medicalisation refers to health professionals carrying out the procedure, which falsely legitimizes a harmful practice. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why is medicalised FGM considered dangerous for the nursing profession?

options.A: It forces nurses to perform surgeries they were not trained to do
options.B: It breaches medical ethics and normalizes a human rights violation
options.C: It increases the cost of treating routine obstetric emergencies
options.D: It causes immediate bankruptcy for local health clinics

explanation: When health workers perform FGM, it violates the core oath to do no harm and normalizes abuse. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h1)

question: A family asks a nurse to perform FGM to ensure social acceptance. What is a primary driver for this request?

options.A: Fear of community ostracization and marital rejection
options.B: Compliance with current World Health Organization guidelines
options.C: Need to prevent congenital abnormalities in newborns
options.D: Desire to treat an active pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Social pressure and the belief that the procedure ensures marriageability drive families to seek out FGM. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why do some families prefer health workers to perform FGM instead of traditional practitioners?

options.A: Government laws actively encourage clinical participation in FGM
options.B: Hospitals offer free surgical services for cultural ceremonies
options.C: They believe sterile tools and anesthesia make the procedure safer
options.D: Traditional practitioners have completely stopped doing the practice

explanation: The false belief in harm reduction through clinical skill pushes families toward medicalised FGM. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which ethical principle is directly violated when a nurse performs FGM?
explanation: Non-maleficence means doing no harm, which is directly breached when a nurse inflicts intentional injury. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h3)

question: What administrative penalty awaits a Nigerian nurse convicted of performing FGM?

options.A: Temporary suspension until community leaders write an apology
options.B: Transfer to a rural primary healthcare center for supervision
options.C: Permanent loss of nursing license and professional deregistration
options.D: A mandatory three-week refresher course in basic wound care

explanation: Regulatory bodies view FGM participation as gross professional misconduct resulting in license revocation. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is a common long-term reproductive complication experienced by survivors of FGM?

options.A: Spontaneous healing of genital tissue before adulthood
options.B: Complete immunity to common sexually transmitted infections
options.C: Obstructed labor and perineal tearing during childbirth
options.D: Increased fertility rates and painless menstrual cycles

explanation: Scar tissue creates rigid blockages in the birth canal, frequently causing obstructed labor. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h4)

question: A patient presents with severe anxiety and flashbacks linked to childhood genital cutting. What does this illustrate?

options.A: Direct neurological damage from local anesthetic agents
options.B: An acute side effect of modern malaria treatment drugs
options.C: Long-lasting psychological trauma caused by the procedure
options.D: A temporary phase of normal adolescent hormonal imbalance

explanation: FGM inflicts profound emotional and psychological scars that persist well into adulthood. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h4)

question: Where can community health nurses best identify young girls at risk of FGM?

options.A: During emergency trauma care for road traffic accidents
options.B: During routine immunization and antenatal care visits
options.C: Through mandatory drug screening in surgical wards
options.D: At annual financial audits in private secondary schools

explanation: Routine maternal and child health clinics provide regular access to families where prevention messages can be shared. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why must nurses actively debunk the myth of safe medicalised FGM?

options.A: To ensure hospitals receive more funding for surgical supplies
options.B: To encourage traditional healers to take over the practice again
options.C: To reduce the workload of midwives in busy labor wards
options.D: To prevent families from seeking out health workers for the cut

explanation: Exposing the falsehood of safe clinical FGM stops families from using health professionals to bypass bans. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the first priority when conducting a physical examination on an FGM survivor?

options.A: Rushing through the assessment to save valuable hospital time
options.B: Involving family members in the physical examination room
options.C: Building trust and explaining every step of the procedure
options.D: Insisting the patient accepts immediate surgical reconstruction

explanation: A trauma-informed approach requires clear communication and consent to prevent triggering past abuse. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h6)

question: A nurse provides care for a survivor experiencing painful intercourse due to scar tissue. What is an appropriate nursing intervention?

options.A: Telling the patient the pain is normal and will disappear soon
options.B: Providing empathetic counseling and referral for specialized care
options.C: Discouraging the patient from seeking any further medical help
options.D: Prescribing strong antibiotics to eliminate the scar tissue

explanation: Survivors need compassionate support and proper referrals to address chronic physical and emotional complications. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h6)
